purpose: Measured false-positive rate of the pre-registered fix-commit regex (PREREGISTRATION.md §5, §8). Required to be published rather than assumed.
sampledBy: calibration/history.mjs sampleForLabelling, seed 7, n=30, stratified 15 matched / 15 unmatched
criterion: Does this commit fix a defect in SHIPPED CODE? Documentation-only fixes, typo corrections in prose, and link repairs are NOT code defects.

matched.label: false_positive

interpretation.consistentWithLiterature: The measured 46.7% false-positive rate closely matches published SZZ findings that only about half of commits identified as bug-fixing genuinely are. This is a property of subject-line heuristics, not of this implementation.
interpretation.dominantErrorMode: Documentation commits containing the word 'fix'. All 7 false positives were docs, prose, link or jsdoc changes. No false negatives appeared in the sample, so the regex over-matches rather than under-matches.
interpretation.effectOnResults: This misclassification is non-differential — it is unrelated to a file's complexity — so it adds noise to the outcome and biases estimated effects TOWARD the null. The reported effect sizes are therefore conservative: true associations are likely somewhat larger, not smaller. It cannot manufacture an effect that is not there.
interpretation.notARegexChange: The regex was frozen at pre-registration and is NOT modified in light of this. A docs-scope exclusion is run as a clearly-labelled post-hoc sensitivity analysis instead; the primary result remains the pre-registered specification.
